confidence_rationale: The canonical statement of the core-knowledge object principles (cohesion, continuity, contact). The CONTINUITY principle -- an object traces exactly one connected path through space and time -- IS the formal content of permanence: an object cannot wink out and reappear, so it must be represented as continuing through occlusion. High mapping fidelity to ARC-006's 'persistent' clause and to the permanence pillar's spatiotemporal-continuity criterion. Confidence below 0.8 because it is a theoretical synthesis (the empirical weight lives in the studies it reviews) and because the principles describe perceptual INPUT analysis, not a memory buffer.
failure_signatures: The principles characterise how infants SEGMENT and INDIVIDUATE objects from surface/motion arrays at perception time; they are not a theory of how an out-of-view object is STORED. ARC-006/MECH-045 must add the buffer that continuity implies but the principles do not themselves specify.

Cohesion (a single bounded contour moving as a connected whole) maps to the object-file UNIT, but REE's z_world is engineered pre-split (MECH-278 'architectural shortcut past stage 2'), so REE currently bypasses the very segmentation the cohesion principle describes.

The principles are deliberately KIND-neutral -- they define 'bounded physical object' without sortal/category content. This is the right level for a token object-file, but it is orthogonal to REE's SD-049 TYPE-tag identity; the two address different questions and should not be conflated.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Infants perceive objects not by Gestalt good-form but by a small set of principles governing material bodies: COHESION (an object is a single bounded entity whose surfaces move as a connected whole), CONTINUITY (an object traces exactly one connected path over space and time, and two objects cannot occupy the same place), and CONTACT (objects act on one another only when they touch). These principles are early-developing and continue to support object representation into adulthood.
mapping.ree_translation: The CONTINUITY principle gives the permanence pillar its formal definition: if an object must trace one connected spatiotemporal path, then when it passes behind an occluder it must be represented as continuing to exist on that path -- permanence is continuity applied across a perceptual gap. COHESION grounds ARC-006's notion of an entity as a 'bounded, bindable structure' and supplies the unit an object-file (MECH-045) keys on. CONTACT connects to the affordance/tools pillar (PILLAR 3). Together they give the object-representation spine a biology-grounded definition of what an object IS, complementing MECH-278's causal-coherence definition.
mapping.mapping_caveat: These are principles for analysing the perceptual INPUT into objects, not a specification of the persistence BUFFER that holds an object out of view. They tell us what the permanence representation must respect (one connected path, one bounded whole), not how it is stored or queried. And they are kind-neutral by design -- they do not address REE's type-tag identity, which is a separate (later-developing) sortal layer.
mapping.source_context: Theoretical synthesis in Cognitive Science integrating habituation and preferential-looking studies of human infants (predominantly 3-5 months) on object segmentation and persistence.

confidence_components.notes: Canonical, field-defining synthesis; source_quality high. Mapping fidelity strong for the continuity=permanence and cohesion=unit links, but it is a review (empirical weight is in the primary studies it cites) and describes perception not storage, so held at 0.72 overall.
